entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Appellant is in detention since 28.03.2023.
3 .

As per the prosecution story, 23 years old prosecutrix moved an application before Police on 28.03.2023 alleging that for the last one and a half year, she was working in Durable Dreams Furniture Show Room Madan Mahal.

entities.text: Durable Dreams Furniture Show Room Madan Mahal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It's owner Deepesh Rathore was having an evil eye on her and was in habit of making bad touch.
On 01.12.2021, when she was alone in the show-room Deepesh Rathore took her in the wash-room and raped her and threatened not to disclose otherwise he will defame her.
Thereafter, he repeatedly raped her, despite knowing that she belongs to Scheduled Caste.
Last time Deepesh committed rape upon her on 24.03.2023.
She being scared of his criminal attitude has quit the job.
FIR was registered.
After investigation charge-sheet has been filed.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Appellant and prosecutrix both are major and they were having consensual sexual relationship.

Learned senior counsel referring number of documents has submitted that appellant has transferred money in the account of prosecutrix and her husband for a number of times and their relations were known to everybody including the husband of the prosecutrix.
Therefore, no offence of rape is made out.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that appellant may be released on bail.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the appellant/accused on the basis of prosecutrix statement recorded under sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
6.
In this case, after investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Both parties are major.
The alleged period of incident is from 21.03.2021 to 24.03.2023.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which appellant may be released on bail.
Consequently, this appeal under Section 14-A (1) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is allowed.

7. It is directed that appellant - Deepesh Rathore be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed Deepesh Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170330537/
2 by it during trial.

entities.text: Deepesh Rathore vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
Appeal is disposed of.
